verdict.rationale: Temporal workflows are authored as code through language SDKs such as TypeScript and Python, with Activities as normal functions. Completed Activity results are not re-run during replay, so execution resumes where it left off after crashes. A hands-on user confirms it models business logic as ordinary code but notes it requires full determinism. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that Workflows are plain code rather than a DSL, first-party documentation of the checkpoint/event-history mechanism, and documented scope of the determinism constraints on workflow code.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I write workflows as ordinary code in my language — steps with automatic checkpointing — not YAML or a proprietary DSL

citations.quote: It models long-running business logic as ordinary code (Workflows) with side effects in Activities, handled by the Temporal runtime.
An Activity is a normal function or method that executes a single, well-defined action
model calls are executed as Activities, so they retry durably and are not repeated during Workflow replay.
guaranteeing that applications resume exactly where they left off after crashes, network failures, or infrastructure outages
a short walkthrough of how to use the Temporal primitives (Activities, Workflows, and Workers) to build and run a Temporal application
